tasks.title: The scheduled run is told which capabilities it holds
tasks.objective: A scheduled run receives a capability catalog built from the person-filtered inheritedToolPolicy.semanticCapabilities on its existing spawn-input field, so an agent is told which grants it holds. Entries gain an invocation union over the four usable binding kinds with a lane-neutral tool reference and, for local CLI, the reviewed argument patterns. The renderer sheds non-granted material first, never hides a grant, and fails the run closed when even names will not fit.
acceptance_criteria: The scheduled spawn input carries a catalog built from the person-filtered capability set, asserted over the real job execution path where the field is absent today
A capability active for the app but not granted to the acting person never appears as ready, asserted with the two sets differing
Rendered guidance carries display name, stable id, neutral tool reference and reviewed argument shape, asserted against exact rendered text
A descriptor is produced for each of the four usable binding kinds; the adapter reference never appears; a legacy mcp_tool binding still fails validation
The neutral reference resolves to the Anthropic tool name against the real projection including with tool search active, and the DeepAgents entry is asserted absent
No grant is hidden: shedding follows the fixed order and the derived ceiling cannot conflict with the never-hide rule
Hard overflow fails the run before any provider or tool call with a redacted capability_catalog_overflow diagnostic naming the counts
The never-hide guarantee survives both the section budget and the total prompt budget, asserted end to end through prompt compilation
A deterministic replay builds materialization through the production path and makes the dispatcher call first, with a negative control proving the descriptor causes it
The 97ded3746 block is gone, the dispatcher description points at the catalog, and its schema, risk and enforcement are pinned unchanged
No descriptor contains an executable path, hash or credential, asserted against a binding carrying all three

required_tests.id: the scheduled spawn input carries a capability catalog
an ungranted but app-active capability never renders as ready
rendered guidance carries name, stable id, lane tool name and reviewed argument shape
a descriptor is produced for each usable binding kind
a capability with several bindings renders every one of them in a deterministic order
a legacy mcp_tool binding never reaches the catalog
a secret-shaped operand is redacted in the rendered catalog, the error text and the audit record
the resolved engine from the worker path selects the Anthropic tool name
the resolved engine from the inline host path selects the Anthropic tool name
a deepagents engine renders no tool name and leaves guidance unchanged
shedding removes requestables, then discovery, then source summaries, then descriptions, then descriptors
the compact grant list survives the total prompt budget
hard overflow aborts the spawn and publishes capability_catalog_overflow before any provider call
hard overflow aborts the inline host spawn and publishes the same diagnostic
the granted capability is the first tool action in replay
removing the descriptor stops the replay producing that call
the dispatcher schema, risk and enforcement are unchanged

reviewer_focus: Which capability set feeds the catalog: the person-filtered inheritedToolPolicy.semanticCapabilities, never the unfiltered snapshot set
That the engine passed to prompt compilation is the resolved model's engine at each call site, not a runtime flag that only distinguishes worker from inline
That the overflow diagnostic is published where the spawn aborts, since the existing startup publisher is never reached
That the shedding order is total over every removable section, so the compact grant list cannot be crowded out
That redaction of a secret-shaped operand covers the rendered catalog, the error text and the audit record
That enforcement is untouched: the 0120 and 0130 proofs stay green

review_budget.reason: Nine source files and seven test files. The task grill widened scope twice: the engine identity is resolved per call site so both prompt-compile callers pass it, and the overflow diagnostic must publish at the abort point because the existing startup publisher runs far later, just before the runner process starts.
